title: Protocol for dissection and culture of murine dorsal root ganglia neurons to study neuropeptide release
protocol: Sacrifice mice using CO2 inhalation, confirming the exposure was lethal.
Lay the mouse on the dissection board in a supine position.
Pin feet down with a needle for stabilization.
Spray 70% ethanol on the fur of the mouse.
Open the chest and expose the heart for perfusion.
Use forceps to pick up the skin around the bottom of the sternum.
Make an incision using a pair of scissors.
Lift the bottom of the sternum with forceps.
Cut along the diaphragm using scissors, holding the forceps high to avoid damage to the heart or lung.
Hold the tip of the scissor ventrally just under the sternum and ribs.
Lift the rib cage and expose the heart.
Cut out a window of the sternum and ribs for better view on the right atrium.
Make an incision on the right atrium to allow blood and perfusion buffer escape.
Hold the heart with forceps.
Pierce the left ventricle at the left apex using the perfusion syringe.
Perfuse with 2–4 mL room temperature PBS.
Turn the mouse to the ventral side.
Pin the mouse to the dissection board again.
Lift the skin at the base of the tail and make an incision over the whole back to the neck.
Pin or cut away the skin on both sides for good access to the back of the mouse.
Make a cut with scissors at the lumbosacral joint to separate the sacrum from the lumbar spine.
Lift the spine with forceps.
Cut through muscles and ribs on the left and right side in cranial direction until the base of the skull.
Cut through the spine at the atlanto-occipital joint.
Remove organs attached to the tissue surrounding the spine.
Place the spine in a 50 mL Falcon tube filled with supplemented HBSS.
Put the tube on ice.
Carefully cut away all surrounding muscle, fat, and other soft tissues using fine bladed scissors.
Be careful not to damage the vertebral column.
Cut away the ribs from the thoracic part of the vertebral column.
Take a small micro-dissection scissor and insert one scissor tip into the caudal spinal canal.
Cut the vertebral column in the sagittal plane from caudal to cranial, one vertebra at a time.
Hold the vertebral column with fingers for better control during cutting.
Ensure cuts are made exactly through the processi spinosi.
Turn the vertebral column and cut through the opposite side again from caudal to cranial, one processus spinosus vertebrae at a time in a sagittal direction.
Split the vertebral column along the sagittal plane.
Take a petri dish filled with supplemented HBSS.
Place both half pieces of the vertebral column in the petri dish to expose the spinal cord.
Hold down one half piece of the vertebral column with one tweezer.
Use another tweezer to grasp the cranial aspect of the spinal cord and carefully pull it out from cranial to caudal.
Repeat the procedure for the other half piece of the vertebral column.
Place the petri dish containing both halves on ice.
Prepare a 15 mL Falcon tube with 15 mL supplemented DMEM media and keep it on ice, leaving the lid open.
Perform the DRG dissection using a stereomicroscope to locate the dorsal root ganglia in the intervertebral foramina connected to the spinal cord through the dorsal root but separated by meninges.
Pin down one half of the vertebral column on a Styr pore pin pad with the spinal canal facing up.
Use fine tweezers to feel between bony vertebrae for intervertebral foramina.
Insert slightly opened tweezer ends into the intervertebral foramen.
Grasp the dorsal and ventral axon roots close to the DRG using tweezers.
Carefully pull the DRG up a few millimeters while maintaining a tight grasp with tweezers.
View through a stereo microscope.
Circle the DRGs under the microscope.
Indicate ventral and dorsal roots with a blue dotted line for orientation.
Grasp the DRG tightly with fine tweezers.
Pull out the DRG from the intervertebral foramen.
Cut away attached axon roots using a spring scissor.
Cut spinal roots and nerves attached to the DRG.
Place the extracted DRG into a 15 mL Falcon tube containing supplemented DMEM.
Discard the vertebral column after collecting all DRGs.
Repeat the process with the other half of the vertebral column.
Optional: Collect DRG into 350 μL of RLT buffer for RNA profiling in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Optional: Collect DRG into 4% Paraformaldehyde (PFA) in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube for microscopy.
Leave the DRG in 4% paraformaldehyde for 6–18 h at 22°C for fixation.
Transfer the fixed DRG from PFA to 15% sucrose solution and incubate at 4°C for 24 h.
Incubate the DRG in 30% sucrose solution at 4°C for at least 24 h or until needed.
Place the DRG in OCT prior to cryostat cutting and store at -80°C for at least 18 h.
Perform all steps in a tissue culture hood.
Place the Collagenase A/Dispase II Mix in a 37°C water bath.
Spin down the DRG in a 15 mL Falcon at 161 × g (1,000 rpm) for 5 minutes.
Remove DMEM carefully using a serological pipette.
Add 3 mL of 37°C Collagenase A/Dispase II mix to the DRG.
Incubate the mixture in a 37°C incubator shaking at around 150 rpm for 15 minutes.
Spin down the mixture at 161 × g for 5 minutes.
Remove the Collagenase A/Dispase II solution carefully using a serological pipette.
Wash the pellet by adding 10 mL DMEM.
Do not resuspend the pellet during washing.
Spin down the sample at 161 × g for 5 minutes.
Remove DMEM carefully using a serological pipette.
Resuspend the pellet in culture media (supplemented Neurobasal media containing cytokines).
Calculate the amount of media needed based on the number of wells to be cultured + 2 × 30 μL (maximum 1 mL).
Take a 1 mL syringe and triturate the DRG solution with an 18 gauge needle by aspirating and ejecting the DRGs in solution 7 times up and down.
Triturate the DRG solution again with a 23 gauge needle, repeating the process of aspirating and ejecting the DRGs 7 times up and down.
Triturate the DRG solution once more with a 28 gauge needle by aspirating and ejecting the DRGs in solution 7 times up and down.
Count cells using a hemocytometer to plate equal cell numbers if comparing different mouse lines or conditions for reproducibility.
Plate neurons at a density of approximately 15,000 neurons per cm².
Remove the laminin droplet from 4 wells using vacuum, leaving only a thin liquid layer.
Immediately plate 30 μL of the cell suspension on the area coated with laminin.
Keep the time between removing the laminin and plating the cell suspension less than 1 minute for each set of 4 wells.
Incubate the plate or wells for 1 hour at 37°C.
Add 200 μL culture media per well in a 96-well plate, 500 μL culture media per well in a 24-well plate, or 2 mL culture media per well in a 2.5 cm petri dish for single wells.
Incubate the plates at 37°C for 18–24 hours.
The cells are ready for experiments after incubation.
Prepare a 10 mg/mL papain solution by dissolving 100 mg papain in 10 mL PBS.
Keep the papain solution on ice.
Prepare two Eppendorf tubes with 1 ml supplemented Neurobasal media without cytokines.
Add 2.5 μL of media only to the unstimulated control tube.
Add 2.5 μL of papain dissolved in PBS (10 mg/mL) to another tube to achieve a 25 μg/mL concentration.
Vortex both tubes for 5–10 s.
Carefully remove the media from 4 wells at a time by bringing the pipette to the edge of the plate where no DRG neurons are attached and slowly aspirate.
Add 200 μL of either unstimulated media or papain containing media to each well by slowly dripping it down the wall of the well.
Incubate for 1 h at 37°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant by placing the pipette on the edge of the plate where no DRG neurons are attached and slowly aspirate.
Pipette the supernatant into a fresh 96 well plate.
Snap freeze the supernatant on dry ice and store at -80°C until ready for Substance P and CGRP ELISA.
Alternatively, keep the supernatant on ice and use it directly.
Follow the manufacturer's instructions for the Substance P ELISA Kit.
Follow the manufacturer's instructions for the CGRP (rat) EIA Kit.
